summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Double fertilization is unique to angiosperms: Syngamy produces the 2n zygote; Triple fusion produces the 3n primary endosperm nucleus (PEN).

conceptBreakdown.content: Angiosperms (*Angion* = vessel; *Sperma* = seed) represent the dominant terrestrial plant group. Ovules are enclosed within a specialized floral structure called the **Ovary**. Upon fertilization, ovules mature into Seeds, while the enclosing ovary transforms into a Fruit.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 8.1 Key Angiospermic Innovations
conceptBreakdown.title: 8.1 Key Angiospermic Innovations
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Flower**: Highly modified reproductive shoot bearing sepals (calyx), petals (corolla), stamens (androecium), and carpels (gynoecium).

2. **Advanced Vascular Systems**: Fully developed **Xylem Vessels** (tracheids + vessel elements with perforated end plates) and **Phloem Companion Cells** paired with sieve tube elements.

3. **Extreme Gametophyte Reduction**:
- **Male Gametophyte**: 3-celled pollen grain (1 vegetative tube cell + 2 male gametes).
- **Female Gametophyte**: 7-celled, 8-nucleate **Embryo Sac** (*Polygonum* type: 3 antipodal cells + 1 central cell with 2 polar nuclei + 1 egg cell + 2 synergids with filiform apparatus).

4. **Loss of Archegonia**: Archegonia are **COMPLETELY ABSENT** in angiosperms.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 8.2 Double Fertilization & Triple Fusion (S.G. Nawaschin, 1898)
conceptBreakdown.title: 8.2 Double Fertilization & Triple Fusion (S.G. Nawaschin, 1898)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
DOUBLE FERTILIZATION
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
   FIRST FERTILIZATION (Syngamy)                   SECOND FERTILIZATION (Triple Fusion)
   1st Male Gamete (n) + Egg Cell (n)              2nd Male Gamete (n) + Central Cell
               │                                   Polar Nuclei (n + n)
               ▼                                               │
        Zygote (2n)                                            ▼
               │                                 Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN, 3n)
               ▼                                               │
         Embryo (2n)                                           ▼
                                                      Endosperm Tissue (3n)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Double fertilization is a diagnostic hallmark unique to Angiosperms. Upon pollen tube penetration into a synergid cell via the filiform apparatus, two male gametes are discharged:

$$\text{Syngamy: } n \text{ (male gamete)} + n \text{ (egg)} \longrightarrow 2n \text{ (diploid zygote)}$$

$$\text{Triple Fusion: } n \text{ (male gamete)} + 2n \text{ (polar nuclei)} \longrightarrow 3n \text{ (PEN / Endosperm)}$$

• **Endosperm Ploidy**: Angiosperm endosperm forms **AFTER FERTILIZATION** and is strictly **TRIPLOID (3n)**, serving as a nutrient-rich storage tissue.
